title: Giving Way on Purpose: Cartesian Impedance for an Arm That Meets a Surface, Admittance for One That Cannot Be Torque Controlled, and Why Each Likes a Different Surface

questions.question: What does Cartesian impedance make the tool?
options: A point that holds its position whatever pushes on it
A spring and damper about the target, in the task's own space
A mass with no stiffness, free to be pushed
A force source that presses with a fixed force
questions.explanation: The wrench at the tool is the stiffness times the pose error less the damping times the velocity, and the Jacobian's transpose turns that into joint torques.

questions.question: With the target 2 cm below the surface, the settled force with stiffnesses 200, 500 and 1000 N/m was:
options: 4.02, 9.75, 19.00 N: the stiffness times 2 cm
20 N for all three, set by the surface
0.02 N for all three
questions.explanation: The force settled to is nearly the stiffness times the 2 cm the target is below the surface. A little less, because the surface itself gives.

questions.question: Peak force on coming down on the surface, stiff against soft:
options: 68.6 N for both, since the speed was the same
questions.explanation: A stiffness of 2000 N/m peaked at 68.6 N and one of 200 N/m at 27.6 N. In the first moment of contact nothing has been measured yet, and the stiffness is all there is.

questions.question: On the stiff surface the admittance with a damper of 100 N s/m was steady (1) or not (0)?
options: 1, steady
1, but only after ringing for a second
It could not be told
questions.explanation: On a surface of 20 000 N/m a damper of 100 N s/m rang. With 1500 N s/m it was steady, and on a soft surface even 100 was.

questions.question: Why is admittance trouble on a stiff surface?
options: The force sensor saturates on a stiff surface
The virtual mass is too small
The delay and the inner loop's lag are inside the loop, and a stiff surface turns a millimetre into a big force
A stiff surface gives no force to measure
questions.explanation: A millimetre of motion changes the force by 20 N. With the measurement and a slow inner loop inside the loop, that gain is too much unless the virtual damper is large.

questions.question: Which is the arm that is torque controlled suited to?
options: Admittance, which needs torque control
Either: they are the same law
Neither: torque control needs a force sensor
Impedance, which is stable on stiff surfaces
questions.explanation: Impedance sends torques, so it needs a torque controlled arm, and it is steady on stiff surfaces. An arm that only takes positions has to use admittance.
